name: Abū Zakariyyā Yaḥyā ibn ʿAlī al-Shaybānī, al-Khaṭīb al-Tibrīzī
summary: Master of language and grammar at the Niẓāmiyya of Baghdad, pupil of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī, commentator on Abū Tammām's Ḥamāsa and the Muʿallaqāt, teacher of al-Jawālīqī.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī counts al-Tibrīzī among the masters of the language and of grammar: he took from Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh al-Raqqī and from Abū Muḥammad al-Dahhān, and taught letters at the Niẓāmiyya in Baghdad, where al-Jawālīqī was his pupil.
He died in Baghdad in 502/1109. His commentaries on the Ḥamāsa, the Muʿallaqāt and the Mufaḍḍaliyyāt were read in the schools.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 443–448
